nodes.title: K3 surfaces
nodes.statement: Over a field k, a K3 surface is a smooth projective geometrically integral surface X/k with ω_X ≅ O_X and H¹(X,O_X)=0. A polarization is an ample invertible sheaf H; it need not be primitive. Base change is part of the structure interface, not a chosen equation for X.
proofSteps: Specialize smooth projective surface geometry and coherent cohomology to these two conditions.
Transport canonical sheaf and cohomology through field extension using proper base change.
acceptance: Dimension is two; geometric integrality is required.

Place the lattice in its own rational span, preserving the integral bilinear form.
acceptance: Arithmetic and geometric ranks are separate invariants.

nodes.title: Primitive cycle classes and the K3 cohomology lattice
nodes.statement: For a K3 surface and ℓ invertible in k, geometric H²_et(X_kbar,Z_ℓ(1)) is free of rank 22, has perfect cup pairing, and Pic(X_kbar)⊗Z_ℓ embeds with torsion-free cokernel. Pic is torsion-free. Over C the integral Betti lattice is even unimodular of signature (3,19), hence has plain determinant square class −1. The arithmetic H² is not identified with geometric H².
proofSteps: Use Kummer and torsion-freeness to obtain the saturated completed first-Chern map.
Use the K3 Betti computation and comparison for rank and pairing; determinant sign is (−1)^19.
acceptance: Use Pic⊗Z_ℓ, not the raw Pic→Z_ℓ-module cokernel.
Check determinant convention is the ordinary Gram determinant.

nodes.title: Lifting Picard data
nodes.statement: A K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 with at most ten line bundles, one ample, admits a projective characteristic-zero lift over a finite flat extension of its Witt ring carrying all those line bundles. A finite-height K3 admits a Picard-preserving lift in the Lieblich–Maulik scope. A finite ramified Witt extension is not replaced by W itself.
proofSteps: For finite height request the Picard-lifting theorem.

For infinite height use the polarized deformation space of dimension 19; imposing s−1 more line bundles cuts by at most s−1 equations. The infinite-height locus has dimension 9, so s≤10 gives a finite-height deformation.
Algebraize with the ample bundle and apply the finite-height case.
acceptance: The ample class is counted among the ten.
W-lifting used in K3.3 is a stronger separate hypothesis.

nodes.title: Uniform NS descent over finite fields

nodes.title: Lifting the auxiliary moduli line bundle
nodes.statement: In the polarized formal K3 deformation used for the Zarhin fourfold, the auxiliary class L on the special moduli fiber lifts through all infinitesimal thickenings and algebraizes. The obstruction is in H²(M_P,O)⊗ I^(j+1)/I^(j+2), with I=(t₁,…,t₁₉); only the first factor has rank one, while the graded quotient has rank binomial(j+19,18).
proofSteps: Use the relative Mukai/determinant correspondence to show that one positive tensor power of the auxiliary L lifts over the entire polarized formal base. This global power-lifting assertion is part of the relative-moduli proof contract.

For I=(t₁,…,t₁₉), the obstruction to the next I-adic thickening lies in H²(O_M_P)⊗ I^(j+1)/I^(j+2). Both factors are finite free over W; multiplication by the positive power exponent is injective, so the obstruction vanishes.
H¹(O)=0 gives compatibility and uniqueness of the lifts. Apply formal effectivity with the ample auxiliary bundle to algebraize. No rank-one assertion about the whole obstruction module is used.
acceptance: A rank-one obstruction-space argument is invalid in 19 variables.

For fixed nonzero d₀∈Q, N>0 and a,b≠0, there are infinitely many odd primes ℓ away from all fixed denominators/discriminants and p such that ℓ≡1 mod N, a,b and 2 are squares modulo every ℓ-power, and a primitive γ∈T(X_k₁,Z_ℓ) has γ²=d₀. The same prime works for all partner indices n.
proofSteps: Take one finite Galois compositum containing the splitting field of the k₀-Frobenius polynomial, i, square roots of d₀, disc NS, 2,a,b, and ζ_N.
Import identity-class Chebotarev infinitude and canonical completions at split places: all eigenvalues and square roots then lie in Q_ℓ.

Apply the reciprocal-eigenvalue discriminant identity to F², where its ±1 eigenspaces correspond to the old ±1 eigenspaces. In rank one this makes the invariant and transcendental discriminants squares; rank≥2 unimodular lattices represent every unit. Discard numerator/denominator primes so d₀ is a unit and γ primitive.
Hensel lifting at odd ℓ lifts the nonzero square residues to all ℓ-powers.
acceptance: Use one common compositum, not separate unrelated infinite prime sets.
A rank-two unimodular lattice need not represent every nonunit; unit representation suffices.

For ℓ∤2d·disc NS and primitive D, v_n is primitive isotropic of rank ℓ^n, its geometric Brauer order is ℓ^n, and its partner X_n is a fine K3 surface. The divisibility ν_n divides 2d, so v_ℓ(disc NS(X_n))=2n+v_ℓ(disc NS(X)), whereas v_p(disc NS(X_n))≤v_p(disc NS(X)).
proofSteps: Compute v_n²=γ²+D²=0 and v_n·(0,D,0)=+2d.
The ℓ-unit norm of γ makes its geometric transcendental reduction primitive. With ℓ∤disc NS, saturation proves exact geometric Brauer order ℓ^n.
The vector (0,D,0) gives the coprime pairing killing the partner gerbe.
Apply the discriminant identity. Since ν_n divides 2d, its ℓ-valuation is zero and its p-contribution only lowers the partner p-valuation.
acceptance: The sign of v_n·(0,D,0) is positive.
Exact geometric Brauer order is proved before automatic stability is used.

nodes.title: The transcendental orthogonal datum of a K3
nodes.statement: Let X/K be a K3 over a number field with all geometric Picard classes defined over K, and σ:K→C. In H²_Betti(X_σ,Z), Pic embeds primitively with signature (1,ρ−1); its rational orthogonal T has signature (2,20−ρ). Set Q_T(x)=−(x,x)_cup/2, so its polar bilinear form is −cup and the Clifford relation is x²=Q_T(x). Choose a lattice L maximal among lattices of T on which Q_T is integral; its signed signature is (b,2), b=20−ρ. Compare the genera for different σ and maximal choices through local realizations, retaining the required dyadic qualifications. The associated period avoids every rational special divisor by Lefschetz (1,1); no maximal Mumford–Tate-group assertion is made.
proofSteps: Apply the K3 Hodge index/signature calculation and primitive embedding.
Take a maximal integral over-lattice in the rational complement using the integral quadratic-lattice supplier; compare local invariants at finite and real places.
A rational vector orthogonal to the period plane would be a rational (1,1) class orthogonal to all of Pic, hence zero.
acceptance: For ρ=1 obtain b=19; for ρ=20 obtain b=0.
